broadcasts.message: normalize.js ready: NFKC, lowercase, collapse whitespace to single ASCII space, trim. Non-string input returns empty string per 'for string input'. No word modifications. Ready for integration.
tokenizer.js implemented: tokenize(text) calls injected normalize, then extracts ASCII alphanumeric runs with interior apostrophes. Tokens are in input order, no filtering. Ready for integration.

pipeline.js ready. processText calls injected tokenize, builds first-seen unique list, and uses Object.create(null) plus hasOwnProperty to avoid constructor issues. Expecting normalize and tokenizer to be faithful.

private_memories.normalizer: Round 1: Starting. Own normalize.js. Spec: NFKC, lowercase, collapse whitespace to single ASCII space, trim. No word changes. Must return string; handle non-string? Spec says 'for string input' — if input not string, return ''. Keep simple. Coordinate with tokenizer (injected normalize) and pipeline. No shadowing. Next: verify with examples.
private_memories.tokenizer: Round 1: I own tokenizer.js. Task: tokenize(text) must call injected normalize(text) exactly once, then extract ASCII alphanumeric runs with interior apostrophes via regex /[A-Za-z0-9]+(?:'[A-Za-z0-9]+)*/g. Keep tokens in order, no stopwords. Ensure no shadowing of normalize. Implement now.
private_memories.integrator: Round 1: I am the integrator. My pipeline.js must define processText(text) that calls injected tokenize(text) and returns {text, tokens, count, unique, frequencies}. Handle prototype names (constructor). No shadowing. Dependencies are in scope. Will keep this memory updated.
